title: Sinus X-ray
what: A standard X-ray of the face. It shows if there is fluid or swelling in your sinuses.
why: For a long-lasting runny nose, pain and pressure in the cheeks and forehead, or a possible sinus infection.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; the report the same or the next day
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you had a sinus X-ray or CT before. Say when

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Jewelry
prepare.text: Take off earrings, hair clips, glasses, and removable dentures.

bring: Past sinus images, if you have them
steps: You stand or sit facing the machine
Your chin rests on a support, with your head tilted back a little
Sometimes you are asked to open your mouth
You keep still for a couple of seconds while the image is taken
feel: It does not hurt. The image takes a fraction of a second
after: You can go about your day right away
The image and report are usually ready the same day. Take them to your ENT doctor

faq.q: Which is more accurate, an X-ray or a CT of the sinuses?
faq.a: CT shows the sinuses in more detail. An X-ray is simpler and faster and is often done first. Your doctor chooses.

faq.q: Can a child have a sinus X-ray?
faq.a: Yes, if a doctor ordered it. The radiation dose is small.

reminders.text: Sinus X-ray soon. Take off earrings and hair clips, and bring your referral.
